full_judgment:
2. The opposite party Nos. 1-6 as plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No. 6 of 1985 before the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Moulvibazar for redemption of mortgage and for khas possession. 

 10. On the other hand, the learned Counsel Mr. Md. Osman Ghani, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1-6 submits at the very out-set that a judgment of affirmance is generally immune from assailed unless it is vitiated by non-consideration and misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case. Next be submits that the plaintiff was examined as P.W. 1 who proved and exhibited the registered sale deed and also the registered Ekrarnama on the same date as exhibits-1 and 2 wherein it has been clearly stated in the Ekrarnama that if the plaintiff would return the entire money within 5 years the defendant will hand over the suit land to the plaintiff. The plaintiff on several occasions offered the defendant to take the entire money and to hand over the suit land to the plaintiff as well as the registered sale deed but the defendant on a false plea filed a suit for specific performance of contract against the plaintiff that the plaintiff again took Tk. 25,000/- as entire valuation of the land and made a oral agreement in presence of the witnesses. Ultimately that suit for specific performance of contract was dismissed for default. Subsequently the plaintiff was constrained to file the instant suit for redemption of mortgage and to recover the khas possession of the suit land. Nurul Mottakim was examined as P.W. 2 who fully supported and corroborated the evidence of P.W. 1. He also submits that although the defendant examined 5 witnesses. D.W. 3 Abdul Motlib was a cousin of the defendant (ফুফাত ভাই) who is highly interested in this case. D.W. 4 Ranu and D.W. 5 Kaptan Mia admitted in their cross-examination that they did not see that the defendant again paid the plaintiff Tk. 25,000/- as consideration money of the entire suit land. The defendant could not produce any scrape of paper or receipt to show that again he paid Tk. 25,000/- to the plaintiff as valuation money over the suit land. He also submits that the evidence of D.Ws are contradictory. As such the claim of the defendant to the effect that subsequent transaction of Tk. 25,000/- was disbelieved by both the Courts below. The learned Counsel finally submits that both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff had been able to prove his case successfully. On the other hand, the defendant miserably failed to prove that again he gave plaintiff Tk. 25,000/-as consideration money to take a regular registered deed from the plaintiff. The concurrent finding of facts cannot be disturbed unless it is manifestly perverse. Hence, the judgment and decree dated 27-2-2002 and 5-3-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Moulvibazar, in Title Appeal No. 76 of 1999 affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court do not call for any interference by this Court.
